_comment: Synthetic-but-realistic captured terminal sessions for the mw-memory recall benchmark. Deterministic: days_old is measured against the fixed NOW in the harness. Any tokens/keys here are OBVIOUSLY fake.

memories.text: cargo build -p camera-driver failed: error[E0308]: mismatched types --> src/frame.rs:88:23 | expected `u16`, found `u32` | the sensor returns a 12-bit value packed in u16 but decode_pixel() handed back u32.
Fixed the E0308 in the camera driver by casting the decoded pixel back to u16 with `as u16` after the shift; the packing math promoted it to u32.
error[E0502]: cannot borrow `self.buffer` as mutable because it is also borrowed as immutable --> src/ring.rs:142. The iterator over self.buffer held an immutable borrow while push() needed &mut.
error[E0277]: the trait bound `Frame: Serialize` is not satisfied --> src/api.rs:31. Forgot to derive Serialize on the Frame struct before returning it as JSON.
error[E0433]: failed to resolve: use of undeclared crate or module `tokio` --> src/main.rs:4. tokio was in dev-dependencies only; moved it to [dependencies].
error[E0716]: temporary value dropped while borrowed --> src/config.rs:52. Bound `let cfg = &load().unwrap();` to a temporary; assigned to a named let first to extend the lifetime.
git push rejected: ! [rejected] main -> main (non-fast-forward). error: failed to push some refs. Remote had commits I did not have; fixed with git pull --rebase then push.
You are in 'detached HEAD' state. git checkout 4586d281 left me detached; recovered with git switch -c hotfix then git switch main.
CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in crates/mw-cli/src/db.rs. Resolved by keeping the incoming schema migration and re-running cargo test.
fatal: refusing to merge unrelated histories when pulling the upstream template. Worked around with git pull origin main --allow-unrelated-histories (one time only).
remote: error: File assets/model.bin is 214.00 MB; this exceeds GitHub's file size limit of 100.00 MB. pre-receive hook declined. Moved the model to Git LFS.
.gitignore not ignoring target/ because it was already tracked. Fixed with git rm -r --cached target && git commit -m 'stop tracking target'.
interactive rebase hit CONFLICT during git rebase -i HEAD~4 while squashing; used git checkout --theirs on Cargo.lock then git rebase --continue.
test test_frame_pipeline::concurrent_decode ... FAILED, then passed on retry. Flaky: a shared static CAMERA_HANDLE was mutated by two tokio tasks without a lock.
Fixed the flaky concurrent_decode test by wrapping CAMERA_HANDLE in a tokio::sync::Mutex; the race was a double &mut across await points.
test server::binds_to_port ... FAILED: Address already in use (os error 48) on 127.0.0.1:8080. A previous run leaked the port; test now binds to port 0 and reads the assigned one.
async test hung then timed out after 60s under `cargo test`; it awaited a channel that was never sent because #[tokio::test] used a single-threaded runtime. Switched to flavor = "multi_thread".
Tests pass locally but fail in CI: test_ordering_dependency relied on an earlier test seeding a temp dir. CI ran tests in a different order; made each test create its own tempdir.
linker error: undefined symbol: sqlite3_open_v2 when building mw-cli. Cause: rusqlite without the `bundled` feature and no system libsqlite3. Added features = ["bundled"].
cross build for aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu failed: linker `aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc` not found. Installed gcc-aarch64-linux-gnu and set CARGO_TARGET_AARCH64... linker.
cargo build --release killed (OOM) during LTO on the Jetson; the 4GB board ran out of RAM. Set lto = "thin" and CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 in the release profile.
error: failed to select a version for `tokio`: multiple versions requested via Cargo.lock. Ran cargo update -p tokio to unify on 1.40 across the workspace.
openssl-sys build failed: Could not find directory of OpenSSL installation. Switched the reqwest dependency to features = ["rustls-tls"] to drop the native OpenSSL requirement.
wasm32-unknown-unknown build failed because chrono used the default `clock` feature which pulls in libc. Disabled default features on chrono for the wasm target.
thread 'main' has overflowed its stack (SIGSEGV) parsing a deeply nested JSON fixture. Worked around by setting RUST_MIN_STACK=8388608 for that test run.
SQLite: no such module: fts5 when creating the search index. The system sqlite lacked FTS5; using rusqlite bundled (compiled with SQLITE_ENABLE_FTS5) fixed it.
SQLite error: database is locked (SQLITE_BUSY) under concurrent writes from the Tauri app and the CLI. Set PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL and a busy_timeout of 5000ms.
cargo clippy failed the build: error: this `.clone()` on a Copy type is redundant. Removed the clone; also fixed a needless_return that clippy flagged with -D warnings.
panic: called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: Os { code: 2, kind: NotFound } when opening memorywhale.sqlite3 — the data dir did not exist yet. Create it with std::fs::create_dir_all first.
docker build failed: COPY failed: no source files were specified because .dockerignore excluded the crates/ directory. Narrowed the .dockerignore pattern.
npm run tauri build failed: Error: spawn cargo ENOENT — the CI image had node but no Rust toolchain. Added rustup to the build image.
brew install failed to fetch bottle for memorywhale-cli: SHA256 mismatch. The Formula sha256 was stale after re-tagging; recomputed it with shasum -a 256 on the tarball.
cargo publish to crates.io failed: error: api errors: crate version 0.4.0 already uploaded. Bumped to 0.4.1 in Cargo.toml before re-publishing.

GitHub Actions release job failed auth: remote: Invalid username or password. The CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN secret was unset; added it (value is the obviously-fake placeholder crates-io-TOKEN-NOT-REAL-000).
AWS S3 upload for the nightly artifact returned 403 SignatureDoesNotMatch. The workflow used a placeholder access key AKIAFAKEFAKEFAKE1234; swapped in the real repo secret reference.
error[E0599]: no method named `as_bytes_mut` found for type `String` in the FTS5 tokenizer shim --> src/search.rs:70. Used as_mut_str().as_bytes() path instead.
test recall::builtin_beats_keyword ... FAILED intermittently because the corpus HashMap iteration order changed the tie-break. Switched to a BTreeMap so ranking ties are deterministic.
